{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVlzVyc8AAAABd5bDSw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BqjeczhHackU", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bqjec", "number": 16, "title": "design: shift Cognix toward a small set of general-purpose coding tools", "body": "## Problem

Cognix currently exposes narrowly scoped file tools (`list_files`, `read_file`, `apply_patch` for unique-span replacement, `create_file`) plus an exact-argv, read-only `run_command`. Extending the agent by adding one specialized tool for every filesystem operation (`delete_file`, `rename_file`, `create_directory`, etc.) risks an ever-growing model tool schema, duplicated security logic, and a limited coding workflow.

We want a **deliberate architectural direction change** inspired by the general-purpose editing and command-execution patterns of coding agents such as [OpenAI Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex), without blindly copying its implementation or weakening Cognix's local-first safety properties.

## Expected outcome

Produce a concrete, implementation-ready **tool architecture proposal** (for example `docs/tool-architecture.md`) and update the relevant development guidance so future work prioritizes a **small set of composable, general-purpose tools** rather than one tool per file operation.

The design should evaluate and specify two primary capabilities:

1. **General-purpose patching:** One coherent patch interface for file additions, updates, deletions and moves, with explicit semantics for parent directories, atomicity, stale-content detection, multi-file changes, rollback/partial success and reviewable previews. Compare a structured patch format, unified diffs and the current `apply_patch`/`create_file` APIs; select and justify a concrete model-facing contract.
2. **Policy-controlled command execution:** A command interface that can eventually handle common development operations (directory creation, search, build/test, Git inspection and, when authorized, project writes). Separate *capability* from *authorization*: define read-only versus write permissions, project-root and Git boundaries, sandbox enforcement, approval UX, network access, executable/argument controls, timeouts, logging and failure behavior. Distinguish the current read-only exact-argv command runner from any proposed write-capable backend.

A suggested long-term shape is `apply_patch` + `exec_command` backed by a shared approval, policy and evidence layer. This is a **design target, not a mandate to expose unrestricted shell access**. Retain specialized tools only where they demonstrably improve reliability or security, and explain the trade-offs.

The design must account for local Ollama models (including `qwen3.8:27b` and `qwen3-coder:30b`) and the practical cost of complex patch schemas on tool-calling reliability.

### Scope boundaries

**This Issue is the architecture/decision and implementation roadmap, not a wholesale rewrite of the working Rust harness.** Do not implement unrestricted shell execution or remove existing tools as part of a documentation-only decision. Propose an incremental migration with independently testable follow-up implementation tasks, preserving existing behavior until replacements are validated.

No desktop UI, MCP integration, multi-agent orchestration, Linux sandbox, automatic Git commits or cloud inference are required by this Issue.

## Context and reproduction

Current `main` inspected at `ff984a96eb338246ab39dc47e7c6324827e425e0`:
- [Tool schemas](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/src/schema.rs): five model-facing tools; `apply_patch` only replaces one unique span in an already-read file; `create_file` adds one new file in an existing directory.
- [Runtime implementation](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/src/runtime.rs): root-anchored descriptor-relative file operations, per-action approval, anti-symlink protections and modification ledger.
- [Implementation/security details](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/docs/implementation.md): macOS Seatbelt read-only verification sandbox, exact command allowlist, and current file operation limits.
- [Agent loop](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/src/agent.rs): sequential tool execution, bounded steps, tool result feedback and evidence reporting.
- [Original MVP scope](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/docs/mvp.md).
- [Development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md).

Motivating workflows: "create a new module directory and source file", "rename a module and update references", "remove an obsolete test", "run a build that writes to a sandboxed build directory". These currently require new dedicated tools or are blocked by the command sandbox.

## Mandatory pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] **AC1 — Current-state analysis:** Document the existing five tools, their actual capabilities, safety invariants, constraints, and how they interact with the agent loop, approvals, command sandbox and evidence. Identify concrete limitations and duplication; do not assert that Codex has identical safety semantics.
- [ ] **AC2 — General patch contract:** Select and specify a model-facing general patch format/API covering add, update, delete and move; define path rules, parent-directory handling, concurrency/stale-state checks, atomicity or explicit partial-success semantics, approvals/previews, and the behavior of malformed or oversized patches. Explain the relationship/migration from existing `apply_patch` and `create_file`.
- [ ] **AC3 — Command capability and policy:** Specify a practical general command execution design with permission classes, user approvals, sandbox isolation, project/Git/network boundaries, write locations (including build outputs), environment sanitization, cancellation/limits, failure-closed behavior, and platform support. State what is *not* safely implementable under the current macOS Seatbelt profile and what new validation would be needed before enabling writes.
- [ ] **AC4 — Shared policy/evidence layer:** Define how tools share approval, tool-call validation, cancellation, action previews, changed-file tracking, verification outcomes and structured failure/denial evidence. Preserve untrusted tool-output treatment and the ability to distinguish a model's claim from recorded execution.
- [ ] **AC5 — Local-model reliability and trade-offs:** Compare a small number of generic tools with multiple narrow tools for Qwen/Ollama use; propose deterministic contract tests and practical real-model evaluations (including malformed patches, multi-file tasks and tool choice) before retiring existing interfaces. Identify compatibility and token/context costs without inventing success rates.
- [ ] **AC6 — Incremental migration plan:** Provide an ordered sequence of implementable follow-up issues/PR-sized milestones with measurable acceptance checks, safe rollback/compatibility strategy, and explicit prerequisites for any write-capable shell mode. The plan should avoid a big-bang replacement and unnecessary parallel abstractions.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation and validation:** Add the architecture decision to repository documentation, link it from README or the appropriate canonical guide, keep historical MVP docs accurate, and validate Markdown, links, docs checker and whitespace using the existing repo tooling. Record actual Pass/Fail/Not run evidence.

## Validation already performed

**Pass (repository inspection):** Inspected the latest `main`, open/closed issues, `src/schema.rs` and `docs/implementation.md`. Confirmed the current narrow tool contracts and no existing Issue specifically addressing this architecture change.

**Not run:** Architecture documentation changes, tests or validation commands. No repository files are modified by creating this Issue.

## Optional validation

Review the proposed patch format against current Codex source and evaluate a small representative set of tool-calling prompts with the two existing Ollama model tags. Record observations and limitations; this is supplementary to the concrete design deliverables.

## Required post-merge verification

None required.
